articleBody:
A beautiful bathroom tile job can fail within months if moisture protection is overlooked. Grout and thin-set mortar are porous, making behind-the-tile waterproofing the real barrier protecting your home. Use this checklist to verify your shower or wet area installation.

- [ ] Deflection-rated subfloor — confirms the floor structure supports the weight of stone or tile without bending.
- [ ] Cementitious backer board — replaces standard drywall in wet areas to provide a stable, moisture-resistant base.
- [ ] ANSI A118.10 waterproof membrane — verifies a continuous liquid-applied or sheet membrane is bonded to the backer board.
- [ ] Pre-sloped shower pan — ensures the floor beneath the waterproof liner pitches toward the drain at a consistent angle.
- [ ] Embedded corner reinforcing tape — covers all wall transitions, joints, and fastener heads with membrane-compatible fabric.
- [ ] 24-hour flood test — tests the shower pan by plugging the drain and filling it with water to verify no leaks before tiling.
- [ ] Modified thin-set mortar — uses a setting adhesive matched specifically to the tile size and substrate type.
- [ ] Movement expansion joints — leaves flexible sealant at wall changes and floor transitions to absorb home settling.

How to use this checklist

Walk through these checkpoints with your tile contractor before tile is set. Confirming that waterproofing passes inspection before thin-set is applied prevents costly mold, rot, and structural repairs later.
